title: Receipts/ClosedGenericStructFromReferencedAssemblyTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (4/4), passes on head (4/4); refutes 2 lens claim(s): requirement-tests-1, requirement-tests-2

refutes.claim: The new report filter lets location-less diagnostics through. `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` reports whenever `!diagnostic.Location.IsInSource`, and `Location.None` is not in source. The two patched sites now build a null location (Location.None) for metadata members (`GetPropertyIdentifierLocation(item)` and `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?...`). So a MemberNeedsKey (MsgPack004, an Error per L2) or BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic about a member of the referenced `Item<T>` is reported in `app` with no location instead of being dropped. If the crashing path in the repro is one of these, the AD0001 crash becomes a build error in `app`, so 'a clean build' is still not met. This also contradicts the method's own remark, the new README/MsgPack004.md text ('reported by the project that defines that type') and L8.

The requirement names three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (reporter lines 735, 1009, 1101). The diff only changes the two in the member loop (new lines ~985 and ~1077). No hunk touches the earlier site in `GetObjectInfo` (~line 735 in 3.1.8). If that index is still unguarded and is reached for a metadata closed generic struct, both the generator (CS8785) and the analyzer (AD0001) still throw IndexOutOfRangeException. The criterion 'diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the symbol has no declaring syntax' would then be unmet.
